description: Security & Sandboxing settings page within the runner Settings panel. Implements the Agent Sandbox Taxonomy (AST) 7-layer defense model: L1 Compute, L2 Resources, L3 Filesystem, L4 Network, L5 Credentials, L6 Actions, L7 Audit. The page provides: (1) a Security Profile selector with three built-in profiles (Permissive, Standard, Strict) and a Custom option that exposes the full policy editor; (2) a Security Posture visualization showing per-layer scores as colored bars; (3) feature toggles for Credential Proxy, Network Mediation, and Security Audit Log; (4) a live Audit Log viewer with filtering, refresh, and JSON export — visible only when audit logging is enabled; (5) an AST educational banner; and (6) Save / Reset buttons. Data is persisted via Tauri IPC commands get_security_settings / update_security_settings. Audit events are fetched from the runner MCP HTTP API at /security/audit/events and /security/audit/summary.

groups.name: Page Structure & Header
groups.description: The Security settings tab renders a page header with a Shield icon, the heading 'Security & Sandboxing', and a subtitle. Below that are the profile selector, security posture visualization, custom policy editor (conditional), features section, audit log viewer (conditional), AST info banner, and action buttons. A loading indicator replaces the form while initial data is being fetched. Error and success banners appear transiently at the top of the form.

assertions.description: The heading 'Security & Sandboxing' is displayed as the page title
The subtitle 'Configure security policies and sandbox constraints for workflow execution' is visible below the heading

criteria.textContent: Configure security policies and sandbox constraints for workflow execution

assertions.description: While settings are being fetched on mount, the form is replaced by a centered message 'Loading security settings...'. Once data is loaded, this message disappears and the full form renders.
assertions.precondition: Settings tab has just been opened and data is still loading

assertions.description: When a save or load operation fails, an error banner with red styling (bg-red-500/10 border-red-500/20 text-red-400) appears above the form displaying the error message. This banner persists until the next save attempt.
assertions.precondition: A save or load operation has failed

groups.name: Security Profile Selector
groups.description: A labeled dropdown lets the user pick from the available built-in profiles (Permissive, Standard, Strict) and a Custom option. Profiles are loaded from the Rust backend via get_security_profiles (returns Vec<ProfileSummary> with name, description, fingerprint). When a built-in profile is selected, a description panel appears below the dropdown showing the profile's description text and its AST fingerprint in monospace format (e.g. 'L1:2/L2:1/L3:1/L4:0/L5:1/L6:1'). Selecting 'Custom' hides the fingerprint panel and reveals the full Custom Policy Editor section.

assertions.description: A label 'Security Profile' is visible above the profile dropdown
A select/combobox element for the security profile is present. The default selection is 'permissive' on first load.

The profile dropdown contains at least four options: the three built-in profiles (Permissive, Standard, Strict) populated from the backend ProfileSummary list, plus a 'Custom' option. Profile names from the backend are used as displayed labels. Selecting a profile from the dropdown immediately updates the Security Posture visualization and either shows the description panel (built-in) or the Custom Policy Editor (custom).

When a built-in profile (permissive, standard, or strict) is selected, a description panel appears below the dropdown. It shows: (1) the profile's human-readable description text; (2) a row labeled 'AST Fingerprint:' with the fingerprint string in a monospace code element (e.g. 'L1:2/L2:1/L3:1/L4:0/L5:1/L6:1' for permissive, 'L1:3/L2:3/L3:3/L4:2/L5:3/L6:3' for standard, 'L1:3/L2:3/L3:3/L4:3/L5:3/L6:3' for strict). This panel is absent when 'Custom' is selected.
assertions.precondition: A built-in profile (permissive, standard, or strict) is selected

groups.name: Security Posture Visualization
groups.description: A 'Security Posture' panel shows a 7-row bar chart, one row per AST layer. Each row has the layer name on the left and 3 colored bar segments representing the security score (0-3). Filled segments represent the current score. Score labels are: 0=None (red), 1=Cooperative (orange), 2=Software (yellow), 3=Kernel (green). Each built-in profile maps to fixed layer scores — Permissive: {L1:2,L2:1,L3:1,L4:0,L5:1,L6:1,L7:1}, Standard: {L1:3,L2:3,L3:3,L4:2,L5:3,L6:3,L7:2}, Strict: all L1-L7 at 3. Custom shows a fixed intermediate visualization.

assertions.description: A heading or label 'Security Posture' is visible as the title of the posture visualization panel
The posture visualization displays all 7 AST layer names: Compute, Resources, Filesystem, Network, Credentials, Actions, Audit. Each name appears in its own row alongside the score bars.
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded and a profile is selected

assertions.description: The posture visualization accurately reflects the selected profile's layer scores. For 'permissive', the Network layer (L4) shows score 0 (None/red — no network restriction) while other layers show scores 1-2. For 'strict', all 7 layers show the maximum score of 3 (Kernel/green). For 'standard', most layers show 3 except Network (L4:2) and Audit (L7:2). Switching profiles immediately updates all 7 layer score bars without a page reload.
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded and a profile is selected

groups.name: Custom Policy Editor — Visibility & Structure
groups.description: The Custom Policy Editor section is only rendered when the Security Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'. It shows a heading 'Custom Policy Editor' (with a Sliders icon) and five sub-sections: Network, Actions, Filesystem, Resources, and Credentials. When any built-in profile is selected, this entire section is hidden.

assertions.description: When a built-in profile (permissive, standard, or strict) is selected, the 'Custom Policy Editor' heading and all its sub-sections are not rendered in the DOM.
assertions.precondition: A built-in profile is selected (permissive, standard, or strict)

assertions.description: When 'Custom' is selected in the profile dropdown, the 'Custom Policy Editor' heading appears along with its five sub-sections: Network, Actions, Filesystem, Resources, and Credentials.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: Switching from a built-in profile to 'Custom' in the profile dropdown immediately renders the Custom Policy Editor. The editor initializes with a default policy: network mode Unrestricted, block_destructive=false, read_only_root=false, no denied paths, no resource limits, credentials mode Direct. Switching back to a built-in profile hides the editor without losing the custom policy values from the component state.

groups.name: Custom Policy Editor — Network Section
groups.description: The Network sub-section of the Custom Policy Editor controls L4 network access. It contains a 'Mode' dropdown (id: security-network-mode) with options: Unrestricted, Allow List, Deny List, Disabled. When 'Allow List' or 'Deny List' is selected, a domains textarea appears for entering one domain per line (supports wildcard patterns like '*.openai.com'). A separate 'Block cloud metadata endpoints' toggle (boolean, default off) controls blocking of cloud provider metadata endpoints regardless of mode.

assertions.description: A select element with id 'security-network-mode' is present in the Custom Policy Editor Network section. Its options are: Unrestricted, Allow List, Deny List, Disabled.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: A domains textarea (labeled 'Allowed domains (one per line)' or 'Denied domains (one per line)') appears only when the network mode is 'Allow List' or 'Deny List' respectively. The textarea has placeholder text 'api.anthropic.com\n*.openai.com' and accepts multi-line domain entries. When mode is 'Unrestricted' or 'Disabled', the textarea is absent.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: A toggle labeled 'Block cloud metadata endpoints' is present in the Network section. It is an independent boolean control that blocks access to cloud provider IMDS/metadata endpoints regardless of the chosen network mode.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

groups.name: Custom Policy Editor — Actions Section
groups.description: The Actions sub-section controls L6 action governance. It contains a 'Block destructive commands' toggle (boolean) and a 'Blocked command patterns (regex, one per line)' textarea (id: security-blocked-commands) with placeholder '^\s*sudo\b\n^\s*su\b'. Command patterns are regex strings matched against command invocations before execution.

assertions.description: A toggle labeled 'Block destructive commands' is present in the Actions sub-section of the Custom Policy Editor.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: A textarea with id 'security-blocked-commands' is present for entering blocked command regex patterns, one per line. The placeholder shows example patterns for sudo and su.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: The Actions policy fields save correctly: regex patterns entered in the blocked commands textarea are stored as an array of strings in the SecurityPolicy.actions.blocked_commands field. The block_destructive toggle maps to actions.block_destructive boolean. These constraints are enforced by the Rust PolicyEngine.evaluate_command() method at workflow execution time.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

groups.name: Custom Policy Editor — Filesystem Section
groups.description: The Filesystem sub-section controls L3 filesystem boundaries. It contains a 'Read-only root filesystem' toggle (boolean) and a 'Denied paths (glob, one per line)' textarea (id: security-denied-paths) with placeholder '/etc/shadow\n/home/*/.ssh/**'. Denied path patterns use glob syntax and are matched against file access attempts during workflow execution.

assertions.description: A toggle labeled 'Read-only root filesystem' is present in the Filesystem sub-section of the Custom Policy Editor.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: A textarea with id 'security-denied-paths' is present for entering denied glob path patterns, one per line. The placeholder shows example patterns for sensitive system paths.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

groups.name: Custom Policy Editor — Resources Section
groups.description: The Resources sub-section controls L2 compute resource limits. It contains a 2×2 grid of number inputs: CPU limit (id: security-cpu-limit, step=0.5, min=0.5, max=16, placeholder='No limit'), Memory in MB (id: security-memory-limit, min=64, max=32768, placeholder='No limit'), PID limit (id: security-pids-limit, min=16, max=4096, placeholder='No limit'), and Timeout in seconds (min=10, max=3600). Empty values mean no limit is applied.

assertions.description: A number input with id 'security-cpu-limit' is present in the Resources sub-section. It accepts values from 0.5 to 16 in steps of 0.5, with placeholder 'No limit'.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: A number input with id 'security-memory-limit' is present in the Resources sub-section. It accepts values from 64 to 32768 (megabytes), with placeholder 'No limit'.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: A number input with id 'security-pids-limit' is present in the Resources sub-section. It accepts values from 16 to 4096, with placeholder 'No limit'.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: The built-in Standard profile uses: 2 CPU, 2048 MB memory, 256 PIDs, 300s timeout. The built-in Strict profile uses: 1 CPU, 1024 MB memory, 64 PIDs, 120s timeout. These values are embedded in the Rust profiles.rs as the canonical policy for each profile — the resource limits are enforced at execution time and not user-configurable when a built-in profile is selected.
assertions.precondition: Standard or Strict profile is selected

groups.name: Custom Policy Editor — Credentials Section
groups.description: The Credentials sub-section controls L5 credential access. It contains a Mode dropdown with three options: 'Direct (current behavior)' — credentials passed through unchanged; 'Proxy (placeholder injection)' — real API keys replaced with placeholder tokens that are rehydrated by a host-side proxy; 'Denied (no credentials)' — all credential access blocked. The Strict built-in profile enforces Proxy mode; Permissive uses Direct.

assertions.description: A select/combobox for credentials mode is present in the Credentials sub-section. Its three options are 'Direct (current behavior)', 'Proxy (placeholder injection)', and 'Denied (no credentials)'.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

assertions.description: The credentials mode option maps to SecurityPolicy.credentials.mode: 'Direct' allows raw API key access; 'Proxy' substitutes keys with placeholder tokens at injection time; 'Denied' returns an error for any credential request. Changing this field in the Custom editor and saving updates the effective policy applied by the Rust PolicyEngine during workflow execution.
assertions.precondition: Profile dropdown is set to 'Custom'

groups.name: Features Section — Toggles
groups.description: A 'Features' section below the profile selector contains three toggle rows, each with a heading and description. The toggles control: (1) Credential Proxy — 'Replace API keys with placeholders; real keys injected by host-side proxy'; (2) Network Mediation — 'Route container network through filtering proxy with domain allowlisting'; (3) Security Audit Log — 'Record policy decisions, network requests, and credential activity'. All three are boolean switches using the ToggleSwitch component with blue-on/neutral-off styling.

assertions.description: A heading or label 'Features' is visible as the title of the Features section
A toggle row with heading 'Credential Proxy' and description 'Replace API keys with placeholders; real keys injected by host-side proxy' is present in the Features section.
A toggle row with heading 'Network Mediation' and description 'Route container network through filtering proxy with domain allowlisting' is present in the Features section.

A toggle row with heading 'Security Audit Log' and description 'Record policy decisions, network requests, and credential activity' is present in the Features section. Enabling this toggle causes the Audit Log Viewer section to appear below the Features section, and triggers an immediate fetch of audit events from GET /security/audit/events.

Each ToggleSwitch has two visual states: checked (bg-blue-600, knob on the right) and unchecked (bg-neutral-600, knob on the left). Clicking a toggle immediately updates the component state via setConfig optimistic update. The change is only persisted when the user clicks 'Save Security Settings'. If saving fails, the toggle state reverts to the last saved value.

groups.name: Audit Retention Field
groups.description: When the Security Audit Log toggle is enabled, an additional 'Audit Retention (days)' labeled number input appears below the three feature toggles, indented with a left border. It accepts values from 1 to 365 days (default: 30). This field is hidden when audit logging is disabled.

assertions.description: The 'Audit Retention (days)' field is not rendered when the Security Audit Log toggle is off.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log toggle is off (audit_enabled=false)

assertions.description: The 'Audit Retention (days)' label and a number input (min=1, max=365) appear below the feature toggles when the Security Audit Log is enabled. The input is visually indented with a left border to signal it is subordinate to the Audit Log toggle.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log toggle is on (audit_enabled=true)

groups.name: Audit Log Viewer — Structure & Controls
groups.description: When audit_enabled is true, an 'Audit Log' section (with a FileSearch icon) appears below the Features section. It contains: a summary badge row (green 'N allowed', red 'N denied', yellow 'N warnings' — warnings badge hidden if 0); a filter dropdown (All / Denied / Allowed / Warnings) with default 'All'; a Refresh button (icon: RefreshCw, spinning while loading, tooltip: 'Refresh audit log'); and an Export button (icon: Download, tooltip: 'Export as JSON') that is only shown when at least one event is in the list. Changing the filter immediately re-fetches from GET /security/audit/events with the corresponding decision query parameter.

assertions.description: The Audit Log section with its heading 'Audit Log' is not rendered when audit_enabled is false.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log toggle is off (audit_enabled=false)

assertions.description: When audit_enabled is true, an 'Audit Log' heading is visible. The section includes a filter dropdown, a Refresh button with title 'Refresh audit log', and an event table.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log toggle is on (audit_enabled=true)

assertions.description: A button with title 'Refresh audit log' is present in the Audit Log viewer controls. Clicking it triggers a fetch to GET /security/audit/events?limit=50 and GET /security/audit/summary. While fetching, the RefreshCw icon spins (animated). After fetch completes, the table updates with new events and summary badges refresh.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log toggle is on (audit_enabled=true)

assertions.description: An Export button (title: 'Export as JSON', icon: Download) is visible only when at least one audit event is in the list. Clicking it fetches all events (GET /security/audit/events?limit=10000), then triggers a browser download of a JSON file named 'security-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.json'.
assertions.precondition: Security Audit Log is enabled and at least one audit event exists

assertions.description: When the audit summary is loaded, three colored badges appear: a green badge showing 'N allowed' (count of allowed decisions), a red badge showing 'N denied', and a yellow badge showing 'N warnings' (only when warnings > 0). Badge counts come from GET /security/audit/summary response fields: allowed, denied, warnings.
assertions.precondition: Audit log is enabled and summary has been loaded

groups.name: Audit Log Viewer — Event Table
groups.description: The audit event table has a sticky header with columns: Time, Type, Decision, Action, Reason. Each row represents one AuditEvent. Time is formatted as toLocaleTimeString(). Type is a badge using EVENT_TYPE_LABELS mapping: policy_evaluation→Policy, capability_grant→Grant, capability_denial→Denial, network_request→Network, filesystem_access→Filesystem, credential_injection→Credential, command_blocked→Command, container_lifecycle→Container. Decision is a colored badge: allowed=green, denied=red, warning=yellow. Action and Reason columns are truncated with title tooltip for overflow. Empty state shows 'No audit events. Click refresh to load.' (or 'Loading...' while fetching).

assertions.description: When no audit events have been fetched yet (before first refresh), the table body shows the message 'No audit events. Click refresh to load.' While a fetch is in progress, it shows 'Loading...' instead.

criteria.textContent: No audit events. Click refresh to load.

assertions.precondition: Audit is enabled, no events loaded yet, and no fetch in progress

assertions.description: Audit event rows use semantic color coding for the Decision column: 'allowed' decisions show a green badge (bg-green-500/20 text-green-400), 'denied' decisions show a red badge (bg-red-500/20 text-red-400), and 'warning' decisions show a yellow badge (bg-yellow-500/20 text-yellow-400). The decision text must match exactly one of these three values from the AuditEvent.decision field.
assertions.precondition: Audit log is enabled and at least one event has been loaded

assertions.description: The Type column displays human-readable labels for event_type values: 'policy_evaluation' → 'Policy', 'capability_grant' → 'Grant', 'capability_denial' → 'Denial', 'network_request' → 'Network', 'filesystem_access' → 'Filesystem', 'credential_injection' → 'Credential', 'command_blocked' → 'Command', 'container_lifecycle' → 'Container'. Unknown event types should still render without crashing.
assertions.precondition: Audit log is enabled and at least one event has been loaded

assertions.description: Changing the filter dropdown (All / Denied / Allowed / Warnings) triggers a re-fetch from GET /security/audit/events with the corresponding decision query param ('all' sends no decision param, others send decision=denied/allowed/warning). The table updates to show only matching events after the fetch completes.
assertions.precondition: Audit log is enabled and at least one event exists

groups.name: AST 7-Layer Info Banner
groups.description: A static informational banner near the bottom of the page (before the action buttons) explains the Agent Sandbox Taxonomy model. It has a blue-tinted background (bg-blue-500/5, border-blue-500/10), an Info icon (blue-400), and text: 'Security policies follow the Agent Sandbox Taxonomy (AST) 7-layer model:' followed by the layer list 'L1:Compute / L2:Resources / L3:Filesystem / L4:Network / L5:Credentials / L6:Actions / L7:Audit'. This banner is always visible regardless of profile or settings.

assertions.description: A banner containing the text 'Agent Sandbox Taxonomy (AST)' is always present on the Security settings page, regardless of which profile is selected.

The AST banner includes the full layer list: 'L1:Compute / L2:Resources / L3:Filesystem / L4:Network / L5:Credentials / L6:Actions / L7:Audit', providing a reference for what each layer code in the fingerprint represents.

groups.name: Action Buttons — Save & Reset
groups.description: Two action buttons appear at the bottom of the form: 'Reset to Defaults' (left, neutral styling) and 'Save Security Settings' (right, blue styling with Shield icon). The Save button cycles through three states: default (Shield icon + 'Save Security Settings'), saving (spinner + 'Saving...', disabled), and success (Check icon + 'Saved', auto-reverts to default after 3 seconds). On save, the Tauri command update_security_settings is invoked with the current config. The backend validates that the profile name is one of permissive/standard/strict/custom, and that custom profile provides a custom_policy.

assertions.description: A 'Reset to Defaults' button is present at the bottom left of the form.
A 'Save Security Settings' button is present at the bottom right of the form with blue styling.

Clicking 'Save Security Settings' initiates a Tauri IPC call to update_security_settings. During the call, the button is disabled and displays a spinner with text 'Saving...'. On success, the button briefly shows a Check icon with text 'Saved' (green), then reverts to the default state after 3 seconds. A success banner (bg-green-500/10 text-green-400) also appears. On failure, an error banner (bg-red-500/10 text-red-400) appears with the error message and the button returns to the default state.

Clicking 'Reset to Defaults' resets the component state to DEFAULT_SETTINGS: default_profile='permissive', custom_policy=null, audit_enabled=false, audit_retention_days=30, credential_proxy_enabled=false, network_proxy_enabled=false. This reset is local only — no API call is made until the user also clicks Save.

The Rust update_security_settings command validates: (1) default_profile must be one of 'permissive', 'standard', 'strict', 'custom'; (2) if default_profile is 'custom', custom_policy must be non-null. If validation fails, the command returns a CommandResponse with success=false and an error message. The frontend displays this message in the error banner and does not show the success state.

transitions.name: Settings loaded with custom profile

states.name: Built-in Profile Selected

transitions.name: Switch to Custom profile

transitions.name: Save built-in profile settings

states.name: Custom Profile Selected
states.description: The 'Custom' profile is selected. The Custom Policy Editor with its five sub-sections (Network, Actions, Filesystem, Resources, Credentials) is visible. The profile fingerprint panel is hidden.

transitions.name: Switch to built-in profile

transitions.name: Auto-dismiss after 3 seconds (built-in profile)
transitions.description: Success state auto-dismisses after 3 seconds, returning to the active profile state
